title: How Zach Yadegari scaled Cal AI to $50M ARR and sold it to MyFitnessPal at 18
summary: Zach explains how Cal AI grew from influencer-only marketing (~$2M/month) to $5.7M/month by adding performance ads and a creator affiliate program. He covers attribution hacks, ad creative, co-founder roles, hiring, and the speed and self-belief mindset behind the exit.

principles.text: Once influencer audiences overlap and saturate, broaden to non-niche creators and add performance ads as a new growth channel.
principles.quote: all of the influencers in the fitness space, all the big ones at least, we'd pretty much worked with and a lot of these fitness influencers share the same audiences. So it was a smaller bang for the buck working with more fitness influencers.

principles.text: Use custom App Store product pages per ad channel to get clean attribution, then gross it up ~30% for people who search the app by name.
principles.quote: you can actually create custom product pages for apps on the App Store. And for each custom product page, you're able to see the amount of revenue that that page by itself generated.

principles.text: Keep ad campaign structure simple and let creative be the strategy; target with creative rather than audience settings.
principles.quote: You want to set up your campaign structures in a very simple way and creative is key. Creative is the whole strategy. You just set it up once and then it's all about the creative.

principles.text: Influencer videos with the app as a subtle cameo cap out in ads; videos dedicated to directly selling the app scaled spend from ~10-15K to ~40K a day.
principles.quote: Then once we started making actual videos where the whole the whole video is dedicated to, okay, this is an app I've been using recently where it lets me track my calories super easily throughout my day.

principles.text: Run an affiliate program where creators make ad-ready videos for a revenue share, instead of directing creative yourself.
principles.quote: we have an affiliate program that lets any creator make videos for us and then they just get a percentage of the revenue. And so we have some creators making a lot of money.

principles.text: Hiring real talent and setting vision matters more than founder hustle once you have product-market fit; speed is the core value.
principles.quote: As soon as we started investing in real talent that's when like the company just started growing on its own.
